title: 18  Abstract Classes
text:
Define an abstract class WorkTool with the fields name of type String and productionYear of type int. Add an abstract method use() that will simulate using the tool. Then define the classes Hammer, Screwdriver and Saw, which inherit from the WorkTool class and implement the use() method. Create an array list of 5 appropriate objects and call the written method for them.
Define an abstract class ComputerGraphic with the fields width, height of type int and fileName of type String. Add the abstract methods loadFile() and saveFile(). Then define the classes Bitmap and Vector, which inherit from the ComputerGraphic class and implement the loadFile() and saveFile() methods. Create an array list of 5 appropriate objects and call the written methods for them.
Define an abstract class ElectronicDevice with the fields manufacturer of type String, model of type String and productionYear of type int. Add the abstract methods turnOn() and turnOff(). Then define the classes Smartphone, Television and Laptop, which inherit from the ElectronicDevice class and implement the turnOn() and turnOff() methods. Create an array list of 5 appropriate objects and call the written methods for them.
In a single project, do the following:

A. Create an abstract class Product containing a public abstract method getPrice() that takes no arguments and returns double. Place the class in the store package.
B. Create two classes derived from Product: Book and Clothing. In both classes, override the getPrice() method. For Book let it return the price 29.99, and for Clothing let it return the price 59.99.
C. In the TestProduct class in the store package, create an array of type Product and initialize it with 5 instances of Book and Clothing. Iterate over the array, calling the getPrice() method for each product (display the prices on standard output).

In a single project, do the following:

A. Create an abstract class Game containing a public abstract method getRating() that takes no arguments and returns double. Place the class in the entertainment package.
B. Create two classes derived from Game: StrategyGame and AdventureGame. In both classes, override the getRating() method. For StrategyGame let it return the rating 8.5, and for AdventureGame let it return the rating 7.3.
C. In the TestGame class in the entertainment package, create an array list of type Game and initialize it with 5 instances of StrategyGame and AdventureGame. Iterate over the array list, calling the getRating() method for each game (display the ratings on standard output).

title: 19  Final Fields, Methods and Classes
text:
Perform the following steps in order:
A. Create a class Planet with one final field name. Try to change the value of the name field after it has been initialized. Analyze the result.
B. Add to the Planet class a method changeName that tries to change the name of the planet. What is the result of trying to change a final field using a method?
Create a class Car with two fields: brand (a regular field) and VIN (a final field - Vehicle Identification Number). Create several Car objects and try to change the VIN field for each of them. Analyze the result.
Create a class Athlete with one final field name and a field points. Create an array of athletes and try to change the name field for one of the athletes. Analyze the result.
Create a class Person with one final field nationalId (national identification number). Then create a class Student that inherits from the Person class. Can you change the nationalId field in the Student class? What happens if you try to do it? Analyze the results.
Create a base class Electronics with a final method turnOn that prints “Device turned on”. Then create a subclass Television and try to override the turnOn method. Observe what happens.
Create a class Computer with a final method boot and a regular method launchApplication. In the subclass Laptop, try to override both methods. Check which of the methods can be overridden and which cannot.
Create a final class ImmutableData with some attributes and methods. Then try to create a subclass VariableData that inherits from the ImmutableData class. Consider why you cannot inherit from a class marked as final.
Create a class Game whose constructor calls a final method initialize (which initializes some data). Create a subclass RPG that tries to customize the constructor of the base class. Make sure that the initialize method works correctly even though it is marked as final.
Create a class MathConstant with a final field PI that is initialized with the value 3.14159. In the subclass PhysicalConstant, try to create a method that tries to change the value of PI. Consider why the value of a final field cannot be changed after it has been initialized.
Perform the following steps:


Create a class ImmutableDate with the private final fields year, month, day.
Add a parameterized constructor to initialize all the fields.
Add the public methods getYear, getMonth, getDay to retrieve the values of the fields, but do not add any methods that allow modifying them.
Implement the methods toString, equals and hashCode.
Check whether such a class can be considered immutable.


Perform the following steps:


Create a class ImmutablePoint with the private final fields x, y, z (the coordinates of the point).
Add a parameterized constructor to initialize all the fields.
Add the public methods getX, getY, getZ to retrieve the values of the fields, but do not add any methods that allow modifying them.
Implement the methods toString, equals and hashCode.
Check whether such a class can be considered immutable.


Perform the following steps:


Create a class ImmutableBook with the private final fields title, author, isbn (ISBN number).
Add a parameterized constructor to initialize all the fields.
Add the public methods getTitle, getAuthor, getIsbn to retrieve the values of the fields, but do not add any methods that allow modifying them.
Implement the methods toString, equals and hashCode.
Check whether such a class can be considered immutable.

title: 20  The Comparable Interface
text:
Write a class Student that contains the fields name (of type String), averageGrade (of type double) and yearOfBirth (of type int). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Student class are sorted in descending order by grade average. Create an array list of 5 objects of the Student class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Write a class Employee that contains the fields name (of type String), salary (of type double) and employmentDate (of type LocalDate). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Employee class are sorted in ascending order by salary. Create an array list of 5 objects of the Employee class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Write a class Client that contains the fields name (of type String), clientNumber (of type int) and lastLogin (of type Date). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Client class are sorted in descending order by the date of last login. Create an array list of 5 objects of the Client class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Write a class Product that contains the fields name (of type String), price (of type double) and productionDate (of type LocalDate). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Product class are sorted in ascending order by production date. Create an array list of 5 objects of the Product class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Write a class Person that contains the fields name (of type String), height (of type int) and dateOfBirth (of type LocalDate). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Person class are sorted in descending order by height. Create an array list of 5 objects of the Person class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Write a class Book that contains the fields title (of type String), numberOfPages (of type int) and publicationDate (of type LocalDate). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Book class are sorted in descending order by number of pages. Create an array of 4 objects of the Book class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Write a class Car that contains the fields brand (of type String), mileage (of type int) and yearOfProduction (of type int). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Car class are sorted in ascending order by mileage. Create an array of 4 objects of the Car class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Write a class FoodProduct that contains the fields name (of type String), price (of type double) and expirationDate (of type LocalDate). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the FoodProduct class are sorted in ascending order by expiration date. Create an array of 4 objects of the FoodProduct class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Write a class Music that contains the fields title (of type String), artist (of type String) and releaseYear (of type int). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Music class are sorted in descending order by release year. Create an array of 4 objects of the Music class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Write a class Item that contains the fields name (of type String), weight (of type double) and price (of type double). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Item class are sorted in ascending order by weight. Create an array of 4 objects of the Item class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Write a class Student that contains the fields name (of type String), averageGrade (of type double) and yearOfStudy (of type int). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Student class are sorted according to a single criterion: in descending order by grade average, and in case of a tie in ascending order by year of study. Create an array of 4 objects of the Student class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Write a class Order that contains the fields productName (of type String), quantity (of type int) and unitPrice (of type double). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Order class are sorted according to a single criterion: in descending order by unit price, and in case of a tie in ascending order by quantity. Create an array list of 4 objects of the Order class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Write a class Client that contains the fields name (of type String), balance (of type double) and lastPurchaseDate (of type LocalDate). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Client class are sorted according to a single criterion: in descending order by balance, and in case of a tie in ascending order by the date of the last purchase. Create an array list of 4 objects of the Client class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Write a class Course that contains the fields name (of type String), numberOfHours (of type int) and price (of type double). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Course class are sorted according to a single criterion: in ascending order by number of hours, and in case of a tie in descending order by price. Create an array of 4 objects of the Course class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Write a class Product that contains the fields name (of type String), price (of type double) and expirationDate (of type LocalDate). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Product class are sorted according to a single criterion: in descending order by expiration date, and in case of a tie in ascending order by price. Create a list of objects of the Product class and sort it according to the specified criterion. Then display the sorted list on the screen.
Write a class Car that contains the fields brand (of type String), model (of type String) and registrationNumber (of type String). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Car class are sorted according to a single criterion: in ascending order by the length of the registration number. Create an array of 4 objects of the Car class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Write a class Employee that contains the fields firstName (of type String), lastName (of type String) and position (of type String). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Employee class are sorted according to a single criterion: in ascending order by the length of the last name. Create an array list of 4 objects of the Employee class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Write a class Movie that contains the fields title (of type String), director (of type String) and genre (of type String). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Movie class are sorted according to a single criterion: in ascending order by the length of the title. Create an array list of 4 objects of the Movie class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Write a class Book that contains the fields title (of type String), author (of type String) and publishDate (of type LocalDate). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Book class are sorted according to a single custom criterion: in ascending order by year of publication. Create an array of 4 objects of the Book class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Write a class Product that contains the fields name (of type String), price (of type double) and productionDate (of type LocalDate). Implement the Comparable interface in such a way that objects of the Product class are sorted according to a single custom criterion: in descending order by year of production. Create an array list of 4 objects of the Product class and sort it according to the specified criterion.
Define a class Client that implements the generic Comparable interface. In this class, declare the private fields lastName of type String and balance of type double. When implementing the compareTo method of the Comparable interface, compare clients based on their balance, and in case of the same balance - based on last name. Then define a class Company that inherits from the Client class. The Company class should additionally have a private field numberOfEmployees of type int. When implementing the compareTo method of the Comparable interface in the Company class, use the compareTo method defined in the Client class and, if necessary, take the numberOfEmployees field into account. Write a program TestClient in which you create an array list of 5 clients and companies named clientList using the ArrayList class. The list should include at least two clients with the same balance and different last names, and two companies with the same number of employees and different balances. Display the contents of clientList, sort it using the instance method sort of the ArrayList class, and display the contents of the list again.
Define a class Animal that implements the generic Comparable interface. In this class, declare the private fields species of type String and age of type int. When implementing the compareTo method of the Comparable interface, compare animals based on their age, and in case of the same age - based on species. Then define a class Dog that inherits from the Animal class. The Dog class should additionally have a private field breed of type String. When implementing the compareTo method of the Comparable interface in the Dog class, use the compareTo method defined in the Animal class and, if necessary, take the breed field into account. Write a program TestAnimal in which you create an array list of 5 animals and dogs named animalList using the ArrayList class. The list should include at least 3 objects of different types.

title: 21  The Comparator Interface
text:

title: 22  Copying Objects
text:
Write a class Student with three fields: name (String), age (int) and grade (double). Implement the Cloneable interface and override the clone() method to be able to clone objects of this class. In the main() method, create a Student object, clone it, and then change the grade (grade) of the original student. Display the grades of both students to see whether they are independent.
Write a class Teacher with three fields: name (String), subject (String) and experience (int). Implement the Cloneable interface and override the clone() method to be able to clone objects of this class. In the main() method, create a Teacher object, clone it, and then change the experience (experience) of the original teacher. Display the experience of both teachers to see whether they are independent.
Write a class Car with three fields: make (String), model (String) and mileage (double). Implement the Cloneable interface and override the clone() method to be able to clone objects of this class. In the main() method, create a Car object, clone it, and then change the mileage (mileage) of the original car. Display the mileage of both cars to see whether they are independent.
Write a class Smartphone with three fields: brand (String), model (String) and productionDate (of type Date). Implement the Cloneable interface and override the clone() method to be able to clone objects of this class. In the main() method, create a Laptop object, clone it, and then change the purchase date (purchaseDate) of the original laptop. Implement the Cloneable interface and override the clone() method to be able to clone objects of this class. In the main() method, create a VideoGame object, clone it, and then change the release date (releaseDate) of the original game. Implement the Cloneable interface and override the clone() method to be able to clone objects of this class. In the main() method, create an Athlete object, clone it, and then change the time at position 3 of the original athlete. Display the times of both athletes to see whether they are independent.
Write a class Teacher with two fields: name (String) and studentsGrades (an array list of variables of type int, representing the grades of each of the students). Implement the Cloneable interface and override the clone() method to be able to clone objects of this class. In the main() method, create a Teacher object, clone it, and then change the grade at position 10 of the original teacher. Display the grades of both teachers to see whether they are independent.
Write a class Teacher with the fields name (String), age (int) and salary (double). Then write a class HeadTeacher that inherits from the Teacher class and adds a field bonus (double). Implement the Cloneable interface and override the clone() method in both classes. In the main() method, show an example demonstrating that objects of these classes are cloned correctly.
Write a class Developer with the fields name (String), age (int) and salary (double). Then write a class SeniorDeveloper that inherits from the Developer class and adds a field bonus (double). Implement the Cloneable interface and override the clone() method in both classes. In the main() method, show an example demonstrating that objects of these classes are cloned correctly.
Write a class Nurse with the fields name (String), age (int) and salary (double). Then write a class HeadNurse that inherits from the Nurse class and adds a field bonus (double). Implement the Cloneable interface and override the clone() method in both classes. In the main() method, show an example demonstrating that objects of these classes are cloned correctly.
Perform the following steps:


Create a class Engine with the fields power, type (engine type) and serialNumber. Add a parameterized constructor and implement the Cloneable interface.
Create a class Car. The Car class should have the fields make, model and engine of type Engine. Add a parameterized constructor and implement the Cloneable interface.

title: 23  Interfaces
text:
Write an interface named LoudAnimal that will have one method named makeNoise(). Then create two classes, Dog and Cat, that will implement this interface. For each class, implement the makeNoise() method so that it prints the appropriate animal sound.
Create an interface named MyComparator that will contain a method compare(int a, int b): int. This method should return -1 if a < b, 0 if a == b and 1 if a > b. Then create a class TestMyComparator that will implement this interface. In this class, implement the compare method according to its description.
Suppose we have an interface MusicPlayer with the methods turnOn(), turnOff() and nextTrack(). Create a class Radio that will implement this interface. The turnOn() method should print the message “Radio turned on”, the turnOff() method - “Radio turned off”, and nextTrack() - “Radio station changed”.
Write an interface Converter with three abstract methods: convertToEuro(double amount) returning double, convertToUSD(double amount) returning double, and getConversionRate(String currency) taking the name of a currency as a String and returning double. Create two classes, CurrencyConverter and UnitConverter, that implement this interface. In a separate class ConverterTest, test the implementation of the methods for objects of both classes.
Create an interface Authentication with three abstract methods: login(String username, String password) returning boolean, logout() returning void, and resetPassword(String username, String oldPassword, String newPassword) returning boolean. Create two classes, UserAuthentication and AdminAuthentication, that implement this interface. In the AuthenticationTest class, test the implementations of the methods for objects of both classes.
Design an interface Sensor with three abstract methods: readValue() returning double, getStatus() returning String, and reset() returning void. Create two classes, TemperatureSensor and PressureSensor, that implement this interface. In the SensorTest class, test how the methods work for objects of both classes.
Develop an interface MediaPlayer with three abstract methods: play(String trackName) returning void, pause() returning void, and getCurrentTrack() returning String. Create two classes, AudioPlayer and VideoPlayer, that implement this interface. In a separate class MediaPlayerTest, check how the methods work for objects of both classes.
Create an interface Storage with three abstract methods: save(String data) returning boolean, delete(String identifier) returning boolean, and retrieve(String identifier) returning String. Design two classes, FileStorage and DatabaseStorage, that implement this interface. In the StorageTest class, test the methods for objects of both classes.
Perform the following steps:


Write an interface DataProcessor with two abstract methods: processData(String data) returning String and isValid(String data) returning boolean.
Create a class TextProcessor that implements DataProcessor. In the processData method, return the data in reverse order, and in the isValid method, check that the data is not an empty string. Make the methods null-safe.
Create a second class NumberProcessor that also implements DataProcessor. In the processData method, return the data with the additional text “Processed:” at the beginning, and in the isValid method, check whether the data is a number.
In the TestDataProcessor class, create objects of both classes and test their methods.

Hint: To check that a string is a number, you can use a regular expression:
str.matches("-?\\d+(\\.\\d+)?")

Perform the following steps:


Create an interface VehicleManager with two abstract methods: startEngine() returning String and getFuelLevel() returning int.
Create a class Car implementing VehicleManager. In the startEngine method return “Car engine started”, and in getFuelLevel return the value 50.
Create a class Motorcycle, also implementing VehicleManager. In startEngine return “Motorcycle engine started”, and in getFuelLevel return the value 30.
In the VehicleManagerTest class, create objects of both classes and test their methods.


Perform the following steps:


Create an interface AnimalSound with one method makeSound().
Extend this interface by creating an interface DomesticAnimalSound that adds a method makeHappySound().
Create a class Dog that implements DomesticAnimalSound. The makeSound() method should return the string “Woof”, and makeHappySound() - “Wag tail”.
In a separate test class (TestAnimals), create a Dog object and call both methods.


Perform the following steps:


Create an interface PowerControl with a method turnOn().
Extend this interface by creating AdvancedPowerControl, which adds a method setPowerSavingMode().
Create a class SmartLamp implementing AdvancedPowerControl. The turnOn() method should activate the lamp, and setPowerSavingMode() should switch it to power-saving mode (the methods should display appropriate messages).
In a separate test class (TestDevices), create a SmartLamp object and call both methods.


Perform the following steps:


Create an interface Drawable with a method draw().
Extend this interface by creating ColorDrawable, which adds a method setColor(String color).
Create a class Circle implementing ColorDrawable. The draw() method should draw a circle, and setColor() should change the color of the circle (the methods should display appropriate messages).
In a separate test class (TestDrawing), create a Circle object, set the color and draw the circle using both methods.


Create an interface Drawable with:


An abstract method draw().
A default method display() that displays the message “Displaying Drawable”.
A static method getType() that returns the String “Drawable Type”.

Create the classes Circle and Rectangle that implement Drawable. draw() in Circle should display “Drawing Circle”, and in Rectangle - “Drawing Rectangle”. Create a test class DrawableTester. Create Circle and Rectangle objects, call draw() and display() on them, and call Drawable.getType() statically.

Create an interface SoundPlayer with:


An abstract method playSound().
A default method stopSound() that displays the message “Sound Stopped”.
A static method getDeviceType() that returns the String “Sound Device”.

Create the classes MusicPlayer and Radio that implement SoundPlayer. playSound() in MusicPlayer should display “Playing Music”, and in Radio - “Playing Radio”. Create a test class SoundTester. Create MusicPlayer and Radio objects, call playSound() and stopSound() on them, and call SoundPlayer.getDeviceType() statically.

Create an interface MemoryManager with:


An abstract method allocateMemory(int size).
A default method freeMemory() that displays the message “Memory Freed”.
A static method getMemoryType() that returns the String “Memory Type”.

Create the classes RAMManager and DiskManager that implement MemoryManager. allocateMemory(int size) in RAMManager should display “Allocating RAM Memory”, and in DiskManager - “Allocating Disk Space”. Create a test class MemoryTester. Create RAMManager and DiskManager objects, call allocateMemory(int size) and freeMemory() on them, and call MemoryManager.getMemoryType() statically.

Create an interface VATCalculator with:


A field double vatRate set to the standard VAT rate (e.g. 23%).
A static method calculateWithVAT(double price) that calculates and returns the price of a product including VAT.

Create a test class VATTest that calls the calculateWithVAT(double price) method with a sample product price and displays the result.

title: 24  Exceptions
text:
Write a program that defines a method checkAge(int age). This method should throw an IllegalArgumentException with an appropriate message if the given age is less than 18. In the main method of the program (main), call checkAge with various values and handle the exception by displaying an appropriate message to the user.
Write a program that asks the user to enter two numbers and then divides the first number by the second. The program should handle two kinds of exceptions: ArithmeticException in the case of division by zero and InputMismatchException when the user enters something other than numbers. In both cases, display an appropriate error message and ask the user to enter the data again. Use the int type.
Design and implement an exception class InvalidDataFormatException that extends the Exception class. Then write a method checkDataFormat(String data) that throws an InvalidDataFormatException if the given string does not match a specific pattern (e.g. it is not an e-mail address). In the main method, test how this method works by handling the exception and informing the user about the error.

title: 25  Generic Programming
text:
Create a simple generic class Box that can store an object of any type. The class should contain a method set to set the object and a method get to retrieve it.
Write a generic method isEqual that takes any two objects of the same type and returns true if they are equal, otherwise false.
Create a generic class Counter<T> that will count the number of added elements of a given type. The class should have a method add(T element) that adds an element to an internal structure, and a method getCount() that returns the number of added elements.
Create a generic class Triple<T, U, V> that can store three objects of different types. Implement the methods getFirst(), getSecond() and getThird() to retrieve the first, second and third element, respectively.
Write a generic method max that takes an array of elements of a comparable type (implementing the Comparable<T> interface) and returns the element with the highest value. Handle the case of an empty array.
Define a generic interface Stack<T> with the methods push(T item), T pop(), T peek() and boolean isEmpty(). Create a class implementing this interface that will represent a stack storing elements of any type.
Create a generic class Storage<T> that stores a single object of any type. The class should have the methods store(T item), which saves the object, and T retrieve(), which returns the stored object.
Write a generic method printArray that takes an array of elements of any type and prints all the elements of the array to standard output. The method should be able to handle arrays of any object type.
Create a generic class Pair that stores two values of any type. The class should have two methods: getFirst(), which returns the first element of the pair, and getSecond(), which returns the second element of the pair.
Write a generic method swap that takes an array of any type and two integers representing indices. The method should swap the elements of the array at the given indices.
Create a generic class GenericQueue<T> that implements a simple queue. The class should have the methods enqueue(T element), which adds an element to the queue, and dequeue(), which removes and returns the element from the front of the queue.
Write a static generic method swap that takes an array of any type and two indices, and then swaps the elements in this array at the specified indices. The method should work for an array of any type. Sample method call: swap(myArray, 0, 2);, where myArray is an array of type Integer[] or any other type. Safeguard the method so that it cannot be called with indices outside the range of the array.
Create a static generic method reverseArray that takes an array of elements of type T and reverses the order of its elements. The method should modify the passed array without returning a new one. Check how the method works on arrays of different types, such as Character, Boolean and your own object types. Safeguard the method so that it cannot be called with a null array.
Write a static generic method minValue that takes an array of elements of a generic type T, where T extends Comparable<T>. The method should return the smallest element of the array. Test this method on arrays containing different types of comparable objects, such as Integer, Double or String. Safeguard the method so that it cannot be called with an array with zero elements. Add a class Person with the fields name and age and test the minValue method on an array of Person objects.
Write a static generic method maxValue that takes an array of elements of a generic type T, where T extends Comparable<T>. The method should return the largest element of the array. Make sure that the method does not accept an empty array (with zero elements). Test the method on arrays containing different types of comparable objects, such as Integer, Float or String. Create a class Vehicle with the fields model and speed, implementing the generic Comparable, and test the maxValue method on an array of Vehicle objects.
Create a static generic method sortAndReturnFirst that takes an array of elements of a generic type T, where T extends Comparable<T>. The method should sort the array and return its first element. Safeguard the method against being called with an empty array (with zero elements). Test this method on various data types, including a newly created class Book with the fields title and author. The Book class should implement the generic Comparable interface based on the title field according to the natural ordering.
Write a static generic method printArray that takes as an argument an array of elements of a generic type T and prints all the elements of the array. Test this method on arrays of type Integer and Double. Then try to test the method on an array of a primitive type, e.g. int or double, and note the resulting compilation errors. Explain why Java does not allow primitive types to be used in the context of generic types.
Create a static generic method sumElements that takes a collection of elements of a generic type T and returns their sum. Test this method on collections of type Integer and Float. Then try to use this method with a collection of primitive types, e.g. int or float, and see what compilation errors appear. Use this to explain the difference between primitive types and object types in Java.
Design a static generic method compareElements that takes two arguments of a generic type T and returns a boolean value indicating whether they are equal. Test the method on pairs of Integer, String and Character objects. Then try to test the same method on primitive types, such as int or char, and describe the problems encountered when trying to use primitive types with generics.
Write a static generic method printObjectInfo that takes an argument of a generic type T with an upper bound of Object. The method should print the object’s class, its hashcode and the result of the toString() method. Test this method on various types of objects, such as String, Integer, and your own classes, e.g. Car, Animal, where each class has its own unique fields and methods.
Create two classes: Animal and Dog, where Dog inherits from Animal. Then write a static generic method findMax that takes two arguments: element1 and element2 of a type that extends Animal. The method should return the larger element according to a comparison criterion you define yourself. In the implementation, compare the elements based on an attribute of your choice, for example age.
Define the classes Car and ElectricCar, where ElectricCar inherits from Car. Write a static generic method compareObjects that takes two arguments: object1 and object2 of a type that extends Car. The method should return true if the objects are of the same type, otherwise false. Use the getClass() method to compare the classes of the objects.
Create a generic class Pair<T> that stores two objects of the same type. Create two classes: Animal and Dog, where Dog inherits from Animal. Then write a static generic method findMax that takes a Pair<? extends Animal>. The method should return the larger element according to a comparison criterion you define yourself.
Create a generic class Triple<T> that stores three objects of the same type. Then create two classes: Bird and Eagle, where Eagle inherits from Bird. Then write a static generic method findMin that takes a Triple<? extends Bird>. This method should return the smallest element based on a comparison criterion you define.
Create a generic class Triple<T> that stores three objects of the same type. Then create two classes: Bird and Eagle, where Eagle inherits from Bird. Then write a static generic method findMin that takes a Triple<? extends Bird>. This method should return the smallest element based on a comparison criterion you define.
Create a generic class ElementPair<T> that stores two objects of the same type. Create two classes: Shape and Circle, where Circle inherits from Shape. Then write a static generic method findLargest that takes an ElementPair<? extends Shape>. The method should return the larger element according to a comparison criterion you define yourself.
Create a generic class DoubleElement<T> that stores two objects of the same type. Create two classes: Person and Student, where Student inherits from Person. Then write a static generic method findYoungest that takes a DoubleElement<? extends Person>. The method should return the smaller element according to your own comparison criterion, for example age.
Create a generic class Pair<T> that stores two objects of the same type. Create two classes: Animal and Dog, where Dog inherits from Animal. The Dog class should have a private field age that the Animal class does not have. Then write a static generic method findMinMaxAge that takes as arguments an array of objects of type Dog and a Pair<?super Dog> result. The method should store (as objects of type Dog) the youngest and the oldest dog (in terms of age) from the array in the second argument of the method. Do this directly, without using the Comparable or Comparator interfaces.
Create a generic class Pair<T> that stores two objects of the same type. Then create two classes: Plant and Tree, where Tree inherits from Plant. The Tree class should have a private field height that the Plant class does not have. Then write a static generic method findMinMaxHeight that takes as arguments an array of objects of type Tree and a Pair<? super Tree> result. The method should store (as objects of type Tree) the shortest and the tallest tree (in terms of height) from the array in the second argument of the method. Also use the generic Comparable interface.

title: 26  Collections
text:
26.1 The Collection Interface
A1. Write a static method printUnique(Collection<T> items) that takes the generic Collection interface as an argument and displays each unique element of this collection on the screen exactly once.
A2. Create a static method countOccurrences(Collection<T> items, T element) that returns the number of occurrences of the given element in the given collection. The function should work for any type of object stored in the collection.
A3. Implement a method removeEveryOther(Collection<T> items) that removes every other element from the passed collection. The method should modify the original collection without creating a copy of it.

title: 26  Collections
text:
26.2 The Iterable Interface
B1. Write a method reversePrint(Iterable items) that takes the generic Iterable interface as an argument and displays the elements of this sequence on the screen in the reverse order to that in which they were passed.
B2. Create a function findMax(Iterable numbers) that searches an Iterable collection containing numbers and returns the largest number. We assume that the elements of the collection are Comparable objects.
B3. Implement a method countElements(Iterable items, Object element) that counts how many times a given element appears in a collection implementing the Iterable interface. The method should compare elements using the equals method.

title: 26  Collections
text:
26.3 The ArrayList Array List
C1. Create a method mergeLists that takes two generic ArrayList<T> and returns a new ArrayList<T> that is the concatenation of the elements of both lists. Make sure that the order of the elements from the original lists is preserved in the resulting list.
C2. Write a function removeDuplicates that takes an ArrayList<T> and returns a new list from which all duplicates have been removed, leaving only unique elements. The order of the retained elements should correspond to their first occurrence in the original list.
C3. Implement a method countOccurrences that takes an ArrayList<T> and an element of type T, and then returns the number of occurrences of this element in the given list.

title: 26  Collections
text:
26.4 The LinkedList Linked List
D1. Write a method isPalindrome that takes a generic linked list (LinkedList<T> list) and returns true if the list is a palindrome, and false otherwise. A list is a palindrome if it reads the same forwards and backwards. The method should be as efficient as possible.
D2. Write a method findCommonElements that takes two generic linked lists (LinkedList<T> list1 and LinkedList<T> list2) and returns a new list containing the elements that occur in both list1 and list2. The elements in the returned list should be unique and do not need to be sorted. The method should not modify the input lists.

title: 26  Collections
text:
26.5 The Hash-Table-Based Set HashSet
E1. Write a method findUniqueElements that takes a generic list (List<T> list) and returns a HashSet<T> that contains only the unique elements of this list. The method should effectively eliminate duplicates.
E2. Write a method hasCommonElements that takes two generic sets (HashSet<T> set1 and HashSet<T> set2) and returns true if both sets have at least one element in common, and false otherwise.
E3. Write a method unionSets that takes two generic collections of type HashSet<T> (HashSet<T> set1 and HashSet<T> set2) and returns a new set (HashSet<T>) that is the union of both input sets. The resulting set should contain all the elements that occur in set1, set2, or in both of these sets.

title: 26  Collections
text:
26.6 TreeSet
F1. Write a method findElementsInRange that takes a TreeSet<T> and two bound values T lowerBound and T upperBound. The method should return a TreeSet<T> that contains all the elements of the original set that fall within the interval between lowerBound and upperBound (inclusive of both bounds).
F2. Write a method removeMinMax that takes a TreeSet<T> and modifies it by removing the smallest and the largest element. The method should return a pair (e.g. a Pair class or a two-element array/list) containing the removed values. If the set has fewer than two elements, the method should return appropriate null values or indicate an error.
F3. Write a method findClosestElement that takes a TreeSet<T> and a value T target. The method should return the element of the set that is closest to the value target. If two elements are equally close, the method may return either of them. We assume that the type T allows values to be compared (e.g. by implementing the Comparable<T> interface).

title: 26  Collections
text:
26.7 Queue
G1. Write a method reverseQueue that takes a generic queue (Queue<T> queue) and reverses the order of its elements. The method should perform the reversal in place, without using additional collections.
G2. Write a method simulateSupermarketQueue that takes a generic queue (Queue<Customer> customers) and a positive integer n representing the number of available checkouts. The Customer class contains the customer’s service time. The method should return the total time needed to serve all customers in the queue, assuming that each checkout serves one customer at a time and takes the next customer from the front of the queue as soon as it becomes free.

title: 26  Collections
text:
26.8 Deque
H1. Write a method isSymmetric that takes a generic Deque (Deque<T> deque) and returns true if the elements in the Deque are arranged symmetrically (i.e. the order of the elements is the same whether we read them from front to back or from back to front). Otherwise, the method returns false.
H2. Write a method removeEverySecondElement that takes a generic Deque (Deque<T> deque) and removes every second element from it, starting with the second element in the order in which the elements were added. The method should modify the original Deque and return nothing.
H3. Write a method swapEnds that takes a generic Deque (Deque<T> deque) and swaps the first element with the last one. If the Deque contains fewer than two elements, the method should do nothing. The method should modify the original Deque and return nothing.

title: 26  Collections
text:
26.9 The PriorityQueue Priority Queue
I1. Write a method mergePriorityQueues that takes two generic PriorityQueues (PriorityQueue<T> queue1 and PriorityQueue<T> queue2). The method should return a new PriorityQueue containing all the elements of both input queues. We assume that the elements in both queues can be compared with each other.

title: 26  Collections
text:
26.10 Map
J1. Write a method reverseMap that takes a generic map (Map<K, V> map) and returns a new map (Map<V, K>), where each key becomes a value and each value becomes a key. If the original map contains repeated values, keep only the last key-value pair when reversing the map.
J2. Write a method findKeysWithMaxValue that takes a generic map (Map<K, V> map), where the values are comparable (implement Comparable<V>). The method should return a list of all keys that are associated with the largest value in the map.
J3. Write a method groupByValue that takes a generic map (Map<K, V> map) and returns a new map (Map<V, List<K>>), where each value from the original map becomes a key in the new map, and its value is the list of keys that were associated with it in the original map.

title: 26  Collections
text:
26.11 HashMap
K1. Write a method countValueOccurrences that takes a generic HashMap (HashMap<K, V> map) and returns a new HashMap (HashMap<V, Integer>), where each key is a value from the original map, and the value is the number of occurrences of that value in the original map.
K2. Write a method swapKeysAndValues that takes a generic HashMap (HashMap<K, V> map) and returns a new HashMap (HashMap<V, K>), where each key from the original map becomes a value and each value becomes a key. We assume that all values in the original map are unique.
K3. Write a method aggregateValuesByKey that takes a generic HashMap (HashMap<K, Integer> map) as well as a key (K key) and a value (Integer value). The method should add the value to the current value associated with the key. If the key does not exist in the map, it should be added with the given value. The method returns nothing and modifies the original map.
K4. Write a method compareMaps that takes two generic HashMaps (HashMap<K, V> map1 and HashMap<K, V> map2) and returns true if both maps have exactly the same key-value pairs, and false otherwise. The method should compare both keys and values.

title: 26  Collections
text:
26.12 TreeMap
L1. Write a method subMapInRange that takes a generic TreeMap (TreeMap<K, V> map) as well as two key values K startKey and K endKey. The method should return a new TreeMap that contains all key-value pairs from the original map whose keys fall within the range from startKey to endKey, inclusive.
L2. Write a method reverseOrderMap that takes a generic TreeMap (TreeMap<K, V> map). The method should return a new TreeMap that contains all key-value pairs from the original map, but with the order of the keys reversed.
Hint: use Collections.reverseOrder().
L3. Write a method calculateAverageValue that takes a generic TreeMap (TreeMap<K, Double> map). The method should calculate and return the average of all values (of type Double) stored in the map. We assume that the map is not empty.

title: 26  Collections
text:
26.13 Vector
M1. Create a function concatenateVectors that takes two Vector<T> objects and returns a new Vector<T> containing all the elements of the first vector, followed by all the elements of the second vector.
M2. Write a method reverseVector that takes a Vector<T> object and returns a new Vector<T> in which the order of the elements is reversed relative to the original vector.
M3. Implement a function filterVector that takes a Vector<T> and the functional interface Predicate<T>. The function should return a new Vector<T> containing only those elements of the original vector that satisfy the condition defined by Predicate<T>.

title: 27  Delegation
text:
Perform the following steps:


Create an interface Printer with a method print(String text).
Create a class StandardPrinter that implements Printer and prints the text to the console.
Create a class Office that has a private field of type Printer. In the Office constructor, take a Printer as an argument and assign it to the field. Add a method printDocument(String text) that will delegate the printing task to the Printer object.


Perform the following steps:


Create an interface Engine with the methods start() and stop().
Create a class PetrolEngine that implements Engine and simulates the operation of a petrol engine.
Create a class Car that has a private field of type Engine. In the constructor, take an Engine as an argument. Add the methods start() and stop(), which will delegate the tasks of starting and stopping the engine, respectively, to the Engine object.


Perform the following steps:


Create an interface Notification with a method send(String message).
Create a class Email that implements Notification and simulates sending an e-mail message.
Create a class User that has a private field of type Notification. In the constructor, take a Notification as an argument. Add a method notifyAboutUpgrade(String information) that will delegate the task of sending the notification to the Notification object.
